title: Incidence and risk factors of running-related injuries during preparation for a 4-mile recreational running event
authors: Buist I, Bredeweg SW, Bessem B, van Mechelen W, Lemmink KA, Diercks RL
population: Novice and recreational runners training for a 4-mile event (Netherlands), 8-week observation
findings: 629 novice and recreational runners were followed for 8 weeks; at least one running-related injury in 25.9%; incidence 30.1 per 1000 h of running (95% CI 25.4 to 34.7).
No previous running experience was the most important risk factor: HR 2.6 (95% CI 1.2 to 5.5) in men and HR 2.1 (95% CI 1.2 to 3.7) in women.
Men were more prone to injury than women (HR 1.4, 95% CI 1.0 to 2.0).
Authors: novice runners may benefit the most from preventive interventions.
limitations: Observational; injury defined as musculoskeletal pain of the lower limb or back restricting running for at least 1 day; the cohort mixes novices and recreational runners; the paper says nothing about dose per session or run-walk.
implications: History is the right axis for splitting start dose: no previous running experience carries roughly double the hazard, which supports separate novice and returner paths.
Do not let sex change the floor dose; the sex-specific HRs are risk profiles, not dosing evidence.
